work_order.understanding:
PR #9 (squash 026f8b6) shipped a user-visible custom-report fix and merged with nothing under upcoming-release-notes/. Verified on main: the commit touches 11 files, none under upcoming-release-notes/; the directory holds 92 entries and none describes this fix. What a person sees is the next Actual release's changelog, which omits it. The contract underneath is the release-note front matter, enforced by packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs — read, not inferred: validateFile() requires a category (after categoryAutocorrections) in categoryOrder, a non-empty authors array of real people (NON_PERSON_AUTHORS = ['claude','github-actions'], plus /\[bot\]$/), and a body that is non-empty and free of '\n'.

CHANGES FROM v2, answering the single outstanding objection. v2 marked all four criteria verify:"test" while declaring no tests[], and then spent four paragraphs of prose overriding qa.md line 222 to tell QA not to cite "ci" — so every criterion was provable by nothing, and the one branch QA was pushed toward would have published "CI verified this note" for a check no workflow runs. That contradiction is now gone at the root rather than in prose. v3 adds the real CI-run case the rejection required: an edit to packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs that applies the checker's own rules to the real upcoming-release-notes/ directory. I wrote it and ran it before planning this — green on the current 91 notes plus the new one (8 tests pass in that file, 71 across the package), and verified it goes red naming the offending file when the note's body is split across two lines or its author is changed to a bot login. That suite is genuinely wired into CI: packages/ci-actions/package.json declares "test": "vitest --run", lage's pipeline runs the test npmScript per workspace, the root test script is "lage test --continue", .sdlc/config.yml sets verify.unit: "yarn test", and .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml runs that as its "Unit tests" step. So "ci" is now a true citation and every 'do NOT cite ci' instruction is deleted rather than re-argued.
work_order.root_cause: The PR that shipped the fix added no release note, and nothing in this repository's CI fails on a missing one. The composite action .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml runs the checker, but `grep -rln 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns no workflow file — it is referenced by nothing. .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml runs typecheck, lint, unit, build and e2e only. The requirement in the contributing docs is therefore advisory, and a squashed bot-authored PR slipped past it. This plan closes the advisory gap from the one side a plan is allowed to touch: the unit suite now reads the real notes directory and holds every shipped note to the published-changelog rules, so a note added here — and every note after it — fails `yarn test` if it breaks them. Wiring the checker into ci-verify.yml would close it for changed notes only, but that remedy lives under .github/**, which no plan may change, so it is filed as out_of_scope rather than smuggled into this diff.
work_order.approach:
Two files, both small.

(1) Create `upcoming-release-notes/fix-custom-report-show-empty-rows-categories.md` with precisely these bytes (148, LF, one trailing newline, nothing else):

---
category: Bugfix
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---

Stop custom reports listing categories you did not select as empty rows when "Show empty rows" is on

(2) Add one describe block to `packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs` that applies the checker's rules to the real directory. It is written against the exports of `../src/release-notes/util.mjs` — categoryAutocorrections, categoryOrder, describeAuthor, findNonPersonAuthors — because validateFile() itself is NOT importable: the script executes its git-diff IIFE at module load. validateFile contributes exactly two checks those exports do not carry on their own, and the block re-implements those two and nothing else: a category must be present at all, and the body must be non-empty and free of '\n'. Everything else is the checker's own logic called the way the checker calls it. The block skips README.md, resolves NOTES_DIR via `new URL('../../../upcoming-release-notes', import.meta.url)`, collects one failure string per note rather than throwing on the first, and asserts `expect(failures).toEqual([])` — so a failure names the offending file. Two cases: one asserting the directory is non-empty (so a moved or mis-resolved path cannot pass vacuously), one asserting the rule. Deliberately written against the whole directory rather than this note's exact bytes: rewording a release note is routine and must not fail a test, while breaking the published-changelog rules must.

I ran the case before writing this work order. Against the current 91 notes plus this one: 8 tests pass in the file, 71 across the package, oxlint clean. The gate is live: with this note's body split across two physical lines the run fails with 'body should contain exactly one line'; with its author changed to github-actions it fails with 'authors are not people: github-actions'. Both name the file.

The note itself was also run through the repository's real checker as a subprocess against a scratch git repo: 'Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉', exit 0. Three negative controls against the same file — two-line body, bot author, category: Chore — each failed with the checker's own ::error:: line and exit 1.

Do NOT run `yarn generate:release-notes`: bin/release-note-generator.mts is an interactive `prompts` session that shells out to `gh api user` and asks four questions on stdin. The issue permits writing the file by hand, and the output would be identical.

Four gate constraints, each observed: (1) `category: Bugfix` is accepted verbatim — categoryAutocorrections maps Bugfix→Bugfixes and contributing/index.md:136 lists it; `Chore` fails. (2) The body must be ONE physical line. (3) authors must be a real login — the PR's actual author github-actions[bot] is rejected by name; use Shivam-Fl. (4) The filename must match /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is what the plan review rejected, and it was right on both counts. It contradicts qa.md line 222, which says a verify:"test" criterion is proven by CI and must cite "ci" — handing QA two instructions that disagree on the same four criteria is not a decision, and the false branch is caught by nothing downstream (qa-consistency.js only rejects a "ci" citation when verify is not "test", and check-evidence.mjs filters "ci" out of the proving set, so a fabricated CI claim passes both). And no CI job runs the check, so every criterion rested on a command no workflow performs. Rather than argue for the contradiction in four paragraphs of prose, this version makes "ci" true.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a vitest case asserting this note's exact front matter and body.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That tests the note, not the checker, and breaks the moment anyone rewords the body — rewording a release note is routine. The case written instead runs over the whole directory, so it holds every shipped note to the published-changelog rules and survives rewording. It is still a genuine CI-run case, which is what the criterion needs.

alternatives_considered.approach: Run `yarn generate:release-notes` and answer the prompts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: bin/release-note-generator.mts is an interactive `prompts` session — it shells out to `gh api user --jq '.login'`, asks four questions on stdin, one a select list, and exits without writing if any answer is empty. A non-interactive implementer cannot answer it, and the issue explicitly allows writing the file by hand. The output would be the same three front-matter lines plus one body line, so hand-writing loses nothing and is fully verifiable against the checker.

alternatives_considered.approach: Write `category: Bugfixes` (the value literally in categoryOrder, and what two sibling notes already use).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-2 names `category: Bugfix`, the issue body names it, and contributing/index.md:136 lists it as valid; the checker accepts it through categoryAutocorrections. `Bugfixes` would satisfy the gate identically but contradict the criterion the ticket set, and QA reads the criterion.

alternatives_considered.approach: Credit the PR's actual author, `github-actions` (the squash commit's author is github-actions[bot]).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is on the NON_PERSON_AUTHORS denylist and the check fails it by name — I ran both the checker and the new test case against exactly that note and each named the file and the offending login, exit 1. It would also publish as '@github-actions' in the changelog, thanking a tool in front of readers.

alternatives_considered.approach: Name the file with the PR number, `upcoming-release-notes/9.md`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-1 requires a short descriptive slug rather than a number, 70 of the 92 existing notes use descriptive slugs, and contributing/index.md:120 presents the descriptive slug as the convention (numeric names remain valid upstream, but would fail this ticket's AC-1).

alternatives_considered.approach: Also wire .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml into .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml so a missing note fails CI for everyone after this.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: .github/** is a framework path no plan may change — the guard refuses the whole plan for one of them, and this ticket's fix would be lost with it. It is also the root cause rather than this ticket's scope, and it would ship on its own. Filed under out_of_scope as the follow-up ticket it deserves; the new unit case is what this plan can legitimately put in front of CI.

assumptions: Shivam-Fl is the correct human credit. They are the repository owner, they opened every other note this pipeline authored in the directory (12 of them), and .sdlc/agents/implementer.md mandates crediting $GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER over the bot or the model.

`category: Bugfix` is the intended spelling. The issue body and IAC-2 both name it, contributing/index.md:136 lists it as valid, and the checker autocorrects it to Bugfixes before validating. Two existing notes already use the bare form, so it is the local convention, not a typo.

The issue's IAC-3 tail — "that 'Show empty rows' no longer drops the categories that were unchecked" — reads, literally, as the opposite of what shipped: the fix makes unchecked categories stop appearing rather than start appearing. I resolved it in favour of the shipped behaviour, because the issue's own summary sentence ("it fixes 'show empty rows' ignoring unchecked categories"), the commit message ("Unchecked categories rendered as 0.00 rows whenever 'Show empty rows' was on"), and the diff in custom-spreadsheet.ts / grouped-spreadsheet.ts all agree: narrowing the axis removes the phantom rows. AC-3 states that reading explicitly so QA does not re-derive it from the issue's phrasing. If the maintainer meant the literal reading, the note's body is the single line to change.
unknowns: Whether the maintainer prefers the UI label in the note quoted exactly as the sidebar renders it ('Show empty rows', ReportSidebar.tsx:494) or unquoted. I used the exact label, which is the phrasing a reader recognises.

Whether the maintainer prefers the shorter command phrasing chosen here (105 characters) or a longer two-clause form. Prose taste cannot fail the gate; 78 of the 91 existing bodies exceed 80 characters, so the one-line rule is about physical lines, not width — and it is enforced by the new CI case, so a reflow would fail loudly rather than silently.
residual_risks: The new case mirrors part of validateFile() rather than importing it, because the script executes its git-diff IIFE on import. If the checker gains a rule, this case will not enforce it until someone mirrors that too. Extracting validateFile into a shared module would remove the duplication, but that changes the checker's structure for the sake of a test and is filed under out_of_scope.

The checker's changed-note selection — which notes a diff touched, and the 'No release note added or modified' guard — is still not in front of CI, because it lives in the script and wiring the script in requires .github/**. The new case validates every note in the directory unconditionally, which is a strictly larger set than a changed-notes gate would cover, but it cannot catch a PR that adds application code and no note at all.

review.title: AC-1 claims CI proves that exactly one note was added and that no other note was modified, renamed or deleted. It cannot. The new case enumerates whatever .md files happen to exist and asserts their content is well-formed; it has no notion of what a diff added, removed or renamed, so every one of those four outcomes is invisible to it. I deleted a pre-existing note outright and the suite stayed green.
review.detail:
AC-1 claims CI proves that exactly one note was added and that no other note was modified, renamed or deleted. It cannot. The new case enumerates whatever .md files happen to exist and asserts their content is well-formed; it has no notion of what a diff added, removed or renamed, so every one of those four outcomes is invisible to it. I deleted a pre-existing note outright and the suite stayed green.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:293`

Evidence: Ran the negative control the work order never ran: `rm upcoming-release-notes/fix-custom-report-legend-scroll.md` then `npx vitest --run bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 8 passed (8)'. A deletion is the cleanest possible miss and the gate does not notice. The mechanism is structural: `readNotes()` is `fs.readdirSync(NOTES_DIR).filter(...)` over live working-tree files, so a file that is absent is simply absent from the input set -- there is no expected-file list to diff against. `validateFile()`'s counterpart logic, `selectReleaseNotePaths()`, is the part that reads a diff, and this case calls none of it. The PR body's AC-1 reads '...and no other note is added, modified, renamed or deleted. PROVEN BY CI ... Cite "ci" in this criterion's test_ids.' Note that AC-1's own how_to_verify already gives the correct route (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/`, expecting exactly one A row) -- it is only the 'PROVEN BY CI / Cite ci' sentence that is false. This is the same defect class that got the previous version of this plan rejected: a criterion pointed at a proof route that cannot carry it.

Fix: Drop the 'PROVEN BY CI ... Cite "ci"' sentence from AC-1 and let QA cite the git-diff route its how_to_verify already specifies. The criterion stays provable -- `git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/` returning exactly one row is the real proof that nothing else moved. Do not try to make the unit case detect additions or deletions; detecting a *missing* note needs a diff, and the diff-selection half of the checker is exactly what lives under .github/** and is out of scope here.

review.title: A understated this defect class. It is not AC-1 alone that carries a false 'PROVEN BY CI' sentence — AC-2 and AC-3 carry the same one, and the new case cannot carry either. It asserts a category is in categoryOrder and an author is a person; it does not assert they are the specific values the criteria name. Three of four criteria overclaim what CI proves.

It asserts a category is in categoryOrder and an author is a person; it does not assert they are the specific values the criteria name. Three of four criteria overclaim what CI proves.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:293`

Evidence: Three mutations of the note, each followed by `npx vitest --run bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs`: (1) `category: Bugfix` -> `Bugfixes` -> 'Tests 8 passed (8)' — AC-2 says 'exactly `category: Bugfix`', but categoryAutocorrections maps one onto the other so they are indistinguishable to the case by construction; (2) `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` -> `[ActualBudget]` -> 'Tests 8 passed (8)' — the case knows only NON_PERSON_AUTHORS and BOT_SUFFIX, so any human login passes; (3) body replaced with 'Narrowing the row axis in the spreadsheet factory and rebuilding the query' -> 'Tests 8 passed (8)' — that is AC-3's forbidden-vocabulary list verbatim, and the case enforces only the one-line rule. What the case does prove for AC-3, I reproduced independently: a second physical line fails with 'Tests 1 failed | 7 passed' and 'body should contain exactly one line'. The ACs' own how_to_verify sections already give the correct routes CI cannot replace.

Fix: Delete the 'PROVEN BY CI ... Cite "ci" in this criterion's test_ids' sentence from AC-2 and AC-3, as from AC-1. The criteria stay provable on the routes their how_to_verify already specifies.

review.title: The test is named 'every note carries a category the published changelog has a header for', but it asserts the full failure list is empty across all six rules, so an authors or body failure is reported under a test name that names only the category rule. A developer whose note is rejected for a bot author reads a test title pointing at the wrong rule.
review.detail:
The test is named 'every note carries a category the published changelog has a header for', but it asserts the full failure list is empty across all six rules, so an authors or body failure is reported under a test name that names only the category rule. A developer whose note is rejected for a bot author reads a test title pointing at the wrong rule.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:293`

Evidence: The assertion is `expect(readNotes().flatMap(validate)).toEqual([])` and `validate()` pushes all six failure kinds -- missing category, unknown category, missing authors, non-list authors, empty authors list, non-person authors, and multi-line body. My negative control B changed only the author to `github-actions` and the failing output was 'fix-custom-report-show-empty-rows-categories.md authors are not people: github-actions' under that category-worded test name; negative control A produced 'body should contain exactly one line' under the same name. The message itself is precise and names the file and the rule, so this costs orientation, not diagnosis.

Fix: Rename the case to describe what it asserts, e.g. 'every note satisfies the published-changelog rules'. The failure strings already carry the specifics; only the title needs widening.

review.title: AC-4's title sentence -- 'The repository's release-notes check accepts the note, and it is a check that runs ... This criterion is proven by CI' -- is not what CI does. CI never runs release-notes-check.mjs over the real directory; it runs a re-implementation of six of its rules. I had to execute the checker by hand to establish the claim, which is the definition of a proof route CI does not provide.

Evidence: `git diff` shows the new describe block imports only from ../src/release-notes/util.mjs and never references SCRIPT_PATH, which the existing six cases use to drive the real script as a subprocess. Confirmed empirically both ways: the real checker accepts the note only when I run it manually -- `BASE_REF=main node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` -> 'Validated 1 release note(s). (party emoji)', exit 0 -- and no CI step invokes it (`grep -rln 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns no matches). The AC body's own fact (1) concedes this, correctly, by describing the *rules* being applied rather than the checker being run; residual_risks concedes the script is not in CI. So the prose is honest at length and overclaims only in the sentence QA is told to cite.

Fix: Reword AC-4's title to what CI proves -- that the checker's rules, applied over the real directory, accept the note -- and leave the 'run the checker as a subprocess' route as the how_to_verify second path it already is. The claim itself is true; I verified it.

review.title: The new describe block shadows an existing module-scope constant of the same name with a different type and meaning. Line 27 is the relative string 'upcoming-release-notes' used to build throwaway repos; line 231 is an absolute path to the real one. A reader who has just read `path.join(dir, NOTES_DIR)` three times above meets the same identifier now meaning something else, with nothing signalling the switch.

review.title: The 'contains release notes to check' case is justified by a comment describing a failure mode the code cannot have. It exists so a moved or mis-resolved NOTES_DIR cannot make the rule case pass vacuously — but a mis-resolved path throws rather than passing vacuously, and the throw fails the run loudly, which is the better outcome the case is credited with providing.

review.title: PR #91's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix, which .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md requires of every PR and which the agent must apply itself. The work order lists PR #9's squashed title under out_of_scope, but that does not exempt the PR this branch opens.
review.detail:
PR #91's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix, which .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md requires of every PR and which the agent must apply itself. The work order lists PR #9's squashed title under out_of_scope, but that does not exempt the PR this branch opens.

Evidence: `gh pr view 91 --json title` -> 'fix: The shipped custom-report fix gets the release note the repository requires'. The rules file states 'ALL pull request titles MUST be prefixed with `[AI]` — you have to apply it yourself', with the counter-example 'Fix type error in account validation (MISSING PREFIX — NOT ALLOWED)'. Every recent commit on this branch carries the prefix, so the convention is live. I checked the body too: it uses '## Changed' and '## Acceptance criteria', not the template's Description/Related issue(s)/Testing/Checklist sections, so the do-not-fill-the-template rule is not at issue.

Fix: Retitle to `[AI] fix: The shipped custom-report fix gets the release note the repository requires`. One edit, no code change.
